spotlights.name: dlt — Distributed Load Tester
spotlights.tagline: Distributed HTTP load tester in Go — correct global tail latency
spotlights.description: A coordinator dispatches work to N horizontally-scaled workers over a custom JSON-over-TCP protocol; they hammer a deliberately-breakable target and their results merge into statistically correct global latency percentiles. Documented like production — every non-trivial decision has an ADR.
bullets: Computes correct global p50/p95/p99 by shipping a serialized HDR histogram from each worker and merging distributions — because the mean of percentiles is not a percentile.
Custom JSON-over-TCP protocol between coordinator and workers: registration, a synchronized start barrier, progress streaming, and result collection.
Built test-first with the race detector on in CI, plus Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards to watch the target degrade under load.

spotlights.name: system-design-maker
spotlights.tagline: Zero-backend system-design tool — custom DSL, live request flow
spotlights.description: Design a system in a small DSL and watch it render as an architecture diagram, then play requests flowing through it in real time — services, queues, and datastores as text, animated end-to-end. Entirely client-side, no backend.
bullets: Custom DSL parsed in the browser into an interactive architecture diagram — define services, queues, and datastores as text and get a live graph.
Animates requests flowing edge-to-edge through the design in real time, so you see how a system behaves rather than just drawing boxes.
Zero-backend and fully static — deployed on GitHub Pages, instant to load and share.

spotlights.name: home-lab
spotlights.tagline: Self-hosted observability stack on a salvaged laptop — akkarilab.xyz
spotlights.description: Infrastructure-as-code for everything running on a home server behind akkarilab.xyz: a Prometheus + Grafana monitoring stack on a salvaged laptop, served publicly through an NGINX reverse proxy. The server pulls straight from the repo — no scattered configs, no copy-paste drift.
bullets: Prometheus + Grafana + node-exporter in Docker Compose, with CPU / memory / disk / network dashboards reachable from anywhere.
NGINX reverse proxy fronts everything on one domain — static landing page, Grafana, and apps routed under akkarilab.xyz over HTTPS.
Everything lives in git and deploys by pull — configs, dashboards, and the landing page are versioned infrastructure, provisioned with Ansible.

spotlights.name: Get equivalently better with less precision
spotlights.tagline: PEFT methods — LoRA & QLoRA — reproduced from scratch · COMP 433
spotlights.description: Two-person deep-learning research project: instead of trusting the papers' numbers, we reimplemented parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods from scratch and benchmarked them on a single RTX 3090.
bullets: Implemented LoRA adapters by hand — modifying Q/K/V projections in PyTorch — and QLoRA (4-bit NF4) for single-GPU fine-tuning of GPT-Neo and Qwen2.5.
Benchmarked accuracy, F1, and VRAM across SST-2, SQuAD v1.1, Wikitext-2, and AlpacaEval — rank-8 LoRA cut GPT-2 perplexity from 54.3 to 31.6.
Full research writeup: proposal, progress report, and final report with training-loss analysis.

spotlights.name: PlayLocal
spotlights.tagline: Location-based platform for organizing local pickup sports
spotlights.description: Find a game nearby, see who's in, and actually show up. 12-person team capstone that won Best Sports App at Concordia's Capstone Expo — built production-shaped: quality gates, coverage tracking, and a real deploy pipeline. I led the team through the full SDLC and owned backend and release engineering across 108 commits.
bullets: Spring Boot backend: auth profiles, Flyway DB migrations, transactional email (Brevo), and CI test configuration.
Reviewed and merged feature work from an AI assistant with knowledge-grounded, user-aware answers to weather forecasts for upcoming games.
Production pipeline: SonarCloud quality gate + Codecov, deployed on Netlify and Render with Neon Postgres.
